subject: markhor goat
title: This Goat's Name Means Snake-Eater. It Has Never Eaten One

scenes.text: This goat's name means snake-eater. It has never eaten a snake.
It's the markhor, Pakistan's national animal, living up to 3,600 meters in the mountains.
Males carry corkscrew horns up to 160 centimeters long, longer than many people are tall.
Folklore said it killed snakes and chewed them. Scientists found no evidence at all.
It eats grass, leaves and twigs, and stands on its hind legs to reach high branches.
The name may really mean snake-horn, after those twisting horns. The snake was on its head all along.

description:
Markhor is often translated from Persian as snake-eater, but this wild goat is strictly herbivorous and there is no evidence it eats snakes.
Pakistan's national animal, males grow corkscrew horns up to 160 cm, and the name may instead mean snake-horn.
What animal name do you think is the most misleading?
first_comment: Markhor numbers have recovered enough that the IUCN moved them to Near Threatened in 2015. Which animal should we myth-bust next?
